paragraphs.text: Repairs dsh-our-free-model at boot: the CodeArts (Huawei Cloud) signed-transport lifetime that broke
after a plugin restart, a dangling injection left by an earlier revision, and the buddy/workbuddy 4
00 (code 11128) attribution User-Agent.
# dsh-tencent-channel-fix
Repairs `dsh-our-free-model` at boot so its channels stay usable, and keeps the repair in place acro
ss upgrades of that plugin and of DeepSeek Harness.
**Revision 2 covers the break that appeared after the DSH upgrade: CodeArts (Huawei Cloud) turns fai
ling with `CodeArts 签名传输已停止` (`code: UNKNOWN`).** That one is a transport-lifetime bug, not a channe
l-gate rejection — see § The CodeArts transport bug.
It still fixes the `400` / `code 11128` returned by the **buddy** and **workbuddy** channels, and re
moves a dangling injection an earlier revision left behind.
> `请求被拦截，请重新发送` · `Illegal API invocation from an unapproved channel` · `INVALID_REQUEST`
## The CodeArts transport bug
`apply()` builds `signedNetwork = createDirectFetch(...)`, registers the CodeArts adapter with `fetc
hImpl: signedNetwork.fetch`, then closes that transport in its own dispose effect.
The adapter stays registered in the kernel's `llm` service, because `registerAdapterIdempotent()` de
liberately keeps the existing route on a duplicate registration (`插件 fiber 重启竞态，保留现有路由并跳过本次注册`).
So once the plugin fiber is disposed and re-created — an OFM hot reload, an in-app upgrade, or a DSH
upgrade that re-applies the profile — every CodeArts request still runs through the **previous** ad
apter, whose fetch points at the **closed** transport. The first call throws and the turn ends.
The repair replaces the captured instance with a closure over a process-wide lane, and rewires all t
hree consumers (auth service, adapter, RPC fetcher). The lane is symbol-keyed on `globalThis`, so it
also survives the module purge OFM performs during a hot reload: an adapter retained from an earlie
r generation follows the successor transport instead of calling into a dead one.
## The buddy / workbuddy channel gate
Tencent's channel gate rejects **two** independent things inside the request. Both must have been fi
xed; fixing one still returned `400`.
> OFM 2.5.9+ retired these channels outright (`isRetiredProvider()` returns true for both), and the
CodeArts-carrying 2.5.8 build no longer contains the `CONTENT_FINGERPRINTS` table the second fix edi
ted. That fix is therefore retired in revision 2; the attribution UA sanitizer is kept because it st
ays correct wherever the channels still exist.
## What is actually wrong
Tencent's channel gate rejects **two** independent things inside the request. Both must be fixed; fi
xing one still returns `400`.
### 1. The attribution User-Agent
`dsh-our-free-model/adapter/kernel.js` publishes the harness identity as the request's `User-Agent`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The `deepseek-harness` token is on the gate's blocklist. The check is **case-insensitive** — `DeepSe
ek-Harness/0.2.1` is rejected too. Every other UA tested was accepted, including `curl`, `node`, `ax
ios`, `undici`, `codex_cli_rs`, `claude-cli`, `opencode`, and the empty UA.
### 2. The harness identity sentence in the system prompt *(historical — fix retired in revision 2)*
DSH's base system prompt opens with:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The gate treats `powered by DeepSeek Harness` as a **content fingerprint** and rejects the whole req
uest when it appears in the system message.
This one is subtle: `dsh-our-free-model` already has a fingerprint-rewriting mechanism (`rewriteTenc
entContentFingerprints`), but it only runs on the **gateway** path (`convertMessage` / `toMessages`)
. The **direct adapter** path — the one `buddy` actually used — assembled its system message with a
bare `messages.unshift(...)` and never called the rewriter. So the sentence went out verbatim.
Measured on the real endpoint (OFM 2.5.7 era, while the Tencent channels still existed):
| Request | Result |

| stock system prompt + stock UA | `400` `code 11128` |
| stock system prompt + fixed UA | `400` `co

de 11128` |
| rewritten system prompt + fixed UA | `200 OK` |
The same gate also rejects `Main branch (you will usually use this for PRs)`, `You are Claude Code,
Anthropic's official CLI for Claude.`, and `x-anthropic-billing-header` — which is why CLI-proxy pro
jects hit the identical error.
Revision 1 patched this by injecting a rewriter call into the direct path. On the pinned 2.5.8 bundl
e that call references a function the bundle no longer contains, so it turned a `400` into a `Refere
nceError`. Revision 2 **removes** that injection (`legacy-direct-rewrite`) and retires the fingerpri
nt-table edit, whose anchor no longer exists upstream.
## Why a plugin, and not a patch
Both defects are text inside `dsh-our-free-model`. Its updater rewrites those files wholesale, so a
hand edit is lost on its next update — **that is exactly how this bug comes back**. It was fixed by
hand once, returned after the plugin updated, and had to be fixed again.
This plugin repairs the two files on every boot instead:
- Written **once**, in `apply()`, before any model request — `pack.js` and `adapter/kernel.js` are i

mported lazily by that plugin on first use, so the write lands well ahead of the module cache.
- **I

dempotent**: a repaired file is detected by marker and left byte-identical.
- **Drift-aware**: if up

stream moves an anchor, that patch is skipped and reported — never forced, never half-written.
- **S
elf-reverting**: files are backed up before writing and `node --check`-ed after; any failure restore
files are backed up before writing and `node --check`-ed after; any failure restores the originals.
An upgrade of `dsh-our-free-model` becomes a self-healing event instead of a regression.
## Compatibility
DSH `>= 0.2.0-rc.1`. Verified against `0.2.0-rc.2` and `0.2.1-rc.2` with `dsh-our-free-model` `2.5.6
If a future `dsh-our-free-model` moves an anchor, `/tencent-fix status` reports the patch as `drifte
d` with the reason, and the repair is skipped rather than forced. Re-derive the anchor from the new
file and bump `PATCHES` in `lib/patcher.js`.
